futureYou.personTheyWillBecome: You will become a credible, employable junior full-stack developer with a portfolio of real, deployed projects that demonstrate React, JavaScript, and backend integration skills — exactly what listings like AgileEngine, Scandiweb, and Compass are hiring for. You will have replaced inflated self-perception with honest, confident positioning that passes technical screens and earns trust in interviews. Within 18 months, you will be a working professional with verifiable experience, growing toward mid-level roles with a salary trajectory that realistically approaches your $10,000/month goal by year three or four.
futureYou.achievementSummary: By the end of this roadmap you will have: 3-5 deployed portfolio projects including at least one React-based frontend and one full-stack application with a real backend; 1-2 open source contributions on GitHub; your first professional junior developer job landed; 12+ months of real work experience on your resume; a professional network of 50+ relevant contacts built through consistent LinkedIn and community engagement; and a mid-level developer promotion or job switch that pushes your compensation significantly above the junior baseline toward your target.

phases.goal: Build a credible, differentiated portfolio and correct the self-positioning that is currently eliminating you before interviews begin
actions: Retire the to-do list app as your lead project immediately and replace it with a deployed full-stack application — for example, a job application tracker with user authentication, a REST API backend in Node.js/Express, and a React frontend — then host it on Vercel or Railway with a live URL in your GitHub README

Build a second portfolio project specifically targeting React jobs listed by employers like Compass and Scandiweb — create a multi-page React app with React Router, component state management using useState and useContext, and at least one third-party API integration such as a weather, movie, or finance API, deployed live

Rewrite your LinkedIn headline, summary, and GitHub profile to honestly and compellingly position you as 'Junior Full-Stack Developer | React, JavaScript, Node.js | Bootcamp Graduate Building Real Projects' — remove all claims of being a senior architect or knowing all languages, which interviewers will probe and expose immediately

Complete one structured credential that fills the 'no verifiable skills' gap: either the Meta Front-End Developer Certificate on Coursera or the full JavaScript course on The Odin Project, and add it with a completion date to your LinkedIn and resume

Make your first open source contribution by finding a beginner-friendly GitHub repository labeled 'good first issue' in the React or JavaScript ecosystem, fixing a bug or improving documentation, and submitting a merged pull request you can reference in applications

Join two active developer communities — the Reactiflux Discord and a local or remote coding meetup — and introduce yourself honestly as a bootcamp grad building toward a junior role, beginning to form relationships before you need referrals
skills: React fundamentals — components, props, state, hooks, and React Router
Node.js and Express REST API development with basic CRUD operations
Git and GitHub — branching, pull requests, and maintaining a clean public profile
Honest professional self-positioning and resume writing for junior developer roles
phases.milestone: Two deployed full-stack or frontend projects are live with public GitHub repos averaging at least 10 meaningful commits each, your LinkedIn has been fully rewritten with accurate positioning, and you have submitted at least 5 job applications to real junior roles from the target list without being screened out for misrepresentation

phases.goal: Land your first junior developer job and accumulate 12 months of real professional experience that makes every future application dramatically stronger
actions: Apply to a minimum of 8-10 junior roles per week from the target listings — specifically tailoring your resume and cover letter to each posting by mirroring the exact technologies they list, such as Angular for the Hirequorum listing or .NET for the Likvido role — tracking every application in a spreadsheet with status, follow-up dates, and feedback received

Prepare specifically for the technical screens used by companies like AgileEngine and Sumsub by solving 3-5 LeetCode easy-to-medium JavaScript problems per week and practicing one mock interview per week using Pramp or interviewing.io, focusing on explaining your thinking out loud

Once employed, identify one internal project or improvement you can own within your first 90 days — even something small like refactoring a component, writing missing documentation, or improving a loading state — and deliver it visibly to build credibility faster than peers

Add TypeScript to your skill set within the first 6 months of employment or during the job search, since the majority of the target listings reference it — convert one of your existing portfolio projects to TypeScript and document the process in a short LinkedIn article

Begin building a public professional presence by posting one LinkedIn update every two weeks about something specific you learned or built — avoid generic posts, instead share a concrete problem you solved and how, which attracts recruiters and hiring managers organically

Expand your portfolio with a third project that demonstrates full-stack capability relevant to the listings — for example, a SaaS-style dashboard with user login, database persistence using PostgreSQL or MongoDB, and a React frontend — targeting the AgileEngine and Junbrain-listed full-stack roles specifically
skills: TypeScript — type annotations, interfaces, and integrating with React projects
Database fundamentals — PostgreSQL or MongoDB with basic querying and schema design
Technical interview performance — JavaScript problem solving and talking through code under pressure
Professional workplace skills — code reviews, Agile ceremonies, Git collaboration in a team environment
phases.milestone: You are employed as a junior frontend or full-stack developer at a company paying at least $4,000/month remote, you have 12 months of continuous professional experience on your resume, and you have shipped at least one feature that is live in a production codebase you can speak to in future interviews

phases.goal: Advance to mid-level and eventually senior developer status, reach your $10,000/month salary target, and build the leadership track record that makes you a genuinely credible senior contributor
actions: At the 2-year mark, initiate a compensation and title review conversation with your manager backed by documented impact — list specific features shipped, performance improvements made, and junior developers you have helped — and either negotiate a raise to mid-level salary or begin a targeted job search at companies known for strong engineering cultures

Take ownership of a meaningful technical initiative at work — propose and lead a migration, introduce a new testing framework, or own a feature from design to deployment — so you have a concrete leadership example to cite in future interviews for mid-level and senior roles

Deepen specialization in one high-value area that matches market demand in the job listings you reviewed — either React performance optimization, full-stack TypeScript with Node.js, or frontend architecture patterns — and make that specialization visible through a GitHub project, a conference talk submission, or a published technical article

Begin mentoring newer developers, either formally at your company or through a bootcamp mentorship program, since senior and lead roles require demonstrated ability to grow others — even one mentee you can speak to specifically will differentiate you from candidates who only have individual contributor experience

Build toward the $10,000/month target by combining base salary growth with strategic job moves — research companies like AgileEngine and Scandiweb that promote from within, target Series A or B startups where equity and fast promotion are common, or explore senior contractor roles which reach that rate faster than salaried positions at large companies
skills: System design fundamentals — component architecture, API design, and scalability thinking appropriate for senior frontend and full-stack roles
Technical leadership — running code reviews, mentoring juniors, and contributing to engineering decisions
Advanced React patterns — performance optimization, custom hooks, state management with Redux or Zustand, and testing with React Testing Library
Career negotiation and personal brand building — salary negotiation, LinkedIn thought leadership, and networking at a senior level
phases.milestone: You are employed as a mid-level or senior developer earning at or above $10,000 per month, you have 3+ years of verifiable professional experience, you have mentored at least one junior developer, and you have led or significantly contributed to one production system that you can describe in detail in any senior-level interview
